newsitem.title: USA: SPS declares regular, merger payouts.
newsitem.headline: SPS declares regular, merger payouts.

text.p: Southwestern Public Service Co said directors Tuesday declared an unchanged quarterly dividend of $0.55 per share on common stock, and a special prorated dividend related to the utility's planned merger with Public Service Co of Colorado (NYSE: PSR).
The regular quarterly dividend is payable June 1, to holders of record May 15.
The special merger-related prorated dividend would accrue at a pre-calculated daily rate from May 16 through the day prior to completion of the planned merger.

If the merger has not been completed on or before Aug. 1, 1997, the declaration of the special dividend will no longer be in effect, SPS said. Instead, the board will reconsider the anticipated merger timing, and declare a dividend and set a new record date, as appropriate.
The board declared a new fiscal year period, changing from a year beginning September 1 to a year beginning January 1.
The company said directors also named new auditors, Arthur Andersen LLP, to audit the consolidated financial statements for the year ending December 31, 1997. The firm replaces Deloite Touche.
Additionally, the board named a new transfer agent, the Bank of New York, effective May 1, 1997.

The pending merger of SPS and Public Service Co. of Colorado, announced in August 1995, is awaiting action by the Securities and Exchange Commission. The merger, which would create New Century Energies, has received all other necessary federal and state regulatory approvals.
